assertions.subject: Alzheimer disease
assertions.quote: Alzheimer disease is the most common cause of dementia, as it is responsible for 70 to 80% of all cases of dementia. It can occur sporadically or be familial

assertions.subject: Vascular dementia
assertions.quote: Vascular dementia accounts for approximately 15% of all dementia cases. Its incidence increases with age and doubles every 5.3 years

assertions.subject: Lewy body dementia
assertions.quote: Lewy body dementia accounts for approximately 5% of dementia cases

assertions.subject: Parkinson disease dementia
assertions.quote: Parkinson disease dementia accounts for approximately 10% of cases of dementia

assertions.subject: Frontotemporal dementia
assertions.quote: Frontotemporal dementia is attributed to 25% of dementia cases in patients older than 65 years of age

assertions.subject: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
assertions.quote: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is rare and occurs in about 1 to 2 cases per million per year globally

assertions.subject: Alzheimer disease
assertions.quote: Alzheimer disease is characterized by widespread atrophy of the cortex and deposition of amyloid plaques, and neurofibrillary tangles of hyperphosphorylated tau protein in neurons, which contribute to their degeneration

assertions.subject: Lewy body dementia
assertions.quote: Lewy body dementia and Parkinson disease dementia are characterized by the intracellular accumulation of Lewy bodies, which are insoluble aggregates of alpha-synuclein protein in the brain

assertions.subject: Frontotemporal dementia
assertions.predicate: deposition of ubiquitinated TDP-43 and hyperphosphorylated tau proteins
assertions.quote: Frontotemporal dementia is characterized by various mutations leading to the deposition of ubiquitinated TDP-43 and hyperphosphorylated tau proteins in the frontal and temporal lobes, leading to dementia, early personality, behavioral changes, and aphasia depending on the subtype

assertions.subject: Huntington disease
assertions.quote: Huntington disease is caused by an autosomal dominant inherited gene mutation
